questions.question: A boat covers 35 km downstream in 2 h and covers the same distance upstream in 7 h. Find the speed (in km/h) of the boat in still water.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Downstream Speed (D) = Distance ÷ Time = 35 ÷ 2 = 17.5 km/h

Upstream Speed (U) = Distance ÷ Time = 35 ÷ 7 = 5 km/h

Speed in Still Water = (D + U) ÷ 2

Speed = (17.5 + 5) ÷ 2 = 22.5 ÷ 2 = 11.25 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 11.25 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance (d) = 35 km

Time taken downstream (td) = 2 h

Time taken upstream (tᵤ) = 7 h

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Downstream speed = u + v

Upstream speed = u − v

(where u = speed of boat in still water and v = speed of stream)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1b658fe064c5094536c6538935585b99656d8e5d21155bc2f0d4af3e96e4e94e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Downstream speed (u + v) = 35 ÷ 2 = 17.5 km/h ---- (1)

⇒ Upstream speed (u − v) = 35 ÷ 7 = 5 km/h ---- (2)

⇒ Adding equations (1) and (2):

⇒ (u + v) + (u − v) = 17.5 + 5

⇒ 2u = 22.5

⇒ u = 22.5 ÷ 2

⇒ u = 11.25 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 11.25 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed of Stream

The speed of the water current or stream (v) is calculated as: v = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

Relative Speed in Boats

When moving downstream, the speeds are added (u+v); when moving upstream, the stream speed is subtracted from the boat speed (u−v).

Ratio of Speeds

If the distance is constant, the ratio of downstream speed to upstream speed is the inverse of the ratio of time taken: D/U = Tᵤ/Td.</p

questions.question: What is the compound interest on a sum of ₹25,000 after three years at a rate of 12 per cent per annum interest compounded yearly?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For a 3-year period, use the interest ratio method 3 : 3 : 1.

First year interest (I₁): 12% of 25000 = 3000

Second year interest on I₁ (I₂): 12% of 3000 = 360

Third year interest on I₂ (I₃): 12% of 360 = 43.2

Total CI = (3 × 3000) + (3 × 360) + (1 × 43.2) = 9000 + 1080 + 43.2 = 10123.2

**∴ The correct answer is ₹10,123.20.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Principal (P) = ₹25,000, Rate (R) = 12% p.a., Time (n) = 3 years.

Formula: Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ and CI = A − P

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/246157f057228286c9e9ed720d82feaf0f7b628b21ff03fefc199ad493093d22.png] 

⇒ A = 25000 × (1 + 12/100)³

⇒ A = 25000 × (1.12)³

⇒ A = 25000 × 1.404928

⇒ A = 35123.2

⇒ CI = 35123.2 − 25000

⇒ CI = 10123.2

**∴ The correct answer is ₹10,123.20.**

**__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

Compound interest is a case of successive percentage increase. For 3 years, the effective rate is [3r + (3r²/100) + (r³/10000)]%.

Difference between CI and SI

For 2 years: Diff = P(R/100)². For 3 years: Diff = P(R/100)² × (3 + R/100).

Compounding Frequency

If interest is compounded half-yearly, the rate is halved (R/2) and the time period is doubled (2n).

questions.question: The LCM of x² − 8x + 15 and x² − 5x + 6 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Factorize the expressions mentally by finding numbers that sum to the middle term and multiply to the last term.

x² − 8x + 15: Numbers are −3 and −5 → (x − 3)(x − 5).

x² − 5x + 6: Numbers are −2 and −3 → (x − 2)(x − 3).

LCM takes all unique factors: (x − 2), (x − 3), and (x − 5).

**∴ The correct answer is (x − 2) (x − 3) (x − 5).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given expressions:

P(x) = x² − 8x + 15

Q(x) = x² − 5x + 6

Factorizing P(x) by splitting the middle term:

⇒ x² − 3x − 5x + 15

⇒ x(x − 3) − 5(x − 3)

⇒ (x − 3)(x − 5)

Factorizing Q(x) by splitting the middle term:

⇒ x² − 2x − 3x + 6

⇒ x(x − 2) − 3(x − 2)

⇒ (x − 2)(x − 3)

The Least Common Multiple (LCM) is the product of all distinct factors of the polynomials, each raised to the highest power it occurs in any of the polynomials.

⇒ LCM = (x − 2)¹ × (x − 3)¹ × (x − 5)¹

**∴ The correct answer is (x − 2) (x − 3) (x − 5).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM and HCF of Polynomials

LCM contains all factors at their maximum power, while HCF (Highest Common Factor) contains only common factors at their minimum power.

The Relationship Property

For any two polynomials f(x) and g(x), the product of the polynomials is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: f(x) × g(x) = HCF(f,g) × LCM(f,g).

Factor Theorem

A polynomial P(x) has a factor (x − a) if and only if P(a) = 0. This can be used to check factors quickly.</p

questions.question: The cost of 3 kg of rice is ₹180. The cost of 8 kg of rice is equal to that of 5 kg of Pulse. The cost of 15 kg of pulses is equal to that of 2 kg of tea. The cost of 3 kg of tea is equal to that of 6 kg of walnuts. What is the cost (in ₹) of 10 kg of walnuts?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Apply Chain Rule for 1 kg Walnut: (180 ÷ 3) × (8 ÷ 5) × (15 ÷ 2) × (3 ÷ 6)

1 kg Walnut = 60 × 1.6 × 7.5 × 0.5 = 96 × 3.75 = ₹360

For 10 kg Walnut: 360 × 10 = ₹3600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3600.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost of 3 kg Rice = ₹180

8 kg Rice = 5 kg Pulse

15 kg Pulse = 2 kg Tea

3 kg Tea = 6 kg Walnuts

**Formula Used:**

Unit Cost = Total Cost ÷ Quantity

Equivalence Cost: QuantityA × PriceA = QuantityB × PriceB

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/abbfb8e86200f194a1ffcb2a4fea0b76f80d10159b2ed663586e1039687f2e7b.png] 

⇒ Cost of 1 kg Rice = 180 ÷ 3 = ₹60

⇒ 5 kg Pulse = 8 kg Rice = 8 × 60 = ₹480

⇒ Cost of 1 kg Pulse = 480 ÷ 5 = ₹96

⇒ 2 kg Tea = 15 kg Pulse = 15 × 96 = ₹1440

⇒ Cost of 1 kg Tea = 1440 ÷ 2 = ₹720

⇒ 6 kg Walnut = 3 kg Tea = 3 × 720 = ₹2160

⇒ Cost of 1 kg Walnut = 2160 ÷ 6 = ₹360

⇒ Cost of 10 kg Walnut = 10 × 360 = ₹3600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3600.**

**__Additional Information__**

Chain Rule in Proportion

It is a method used to find a relationship between multiple quantities. The formula is: (Item₁/Item₂) × (Item₂/Item₃) × ... × (Itemₙ−₁/Itemₙ).

Unitary Method

To solve such problems, always find the value of a single unit (1 kg) for each commodity before moving to the next level in the hierarchy.

Inverse Proportion

If the quantity increases while the total cost remains constant, the unit price must decrease: Price ∝ 1 ÷ Quantity.

questions.question: What is the ratio of the simple interest earned on a certain amount at the rate of 21% per annum for 8 years to that earned on the same sum at the same rate for 21 years?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Since the Principal (P) and the Rate of Interest (R) are the same for both cases, Simple Interest (SI) is directly proportional to Time (T).

SI ∝ T (when P and R are constant)

Ratio of Interest = Ratio of Time = T₁ : T₂

Ratio = 8 : 21

**∴ The correct answer is 8 : 21.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P₁) = Principal (P₂) = P

Rate (R₁) = Rate (R₂) = 21%

Time (T₁) = 8 years

Time (T₂) = 21 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c45a3bcbe90770e4fb8fe374cf4c2e6d80720303b94252baef7dbf293cf6b880.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI₁ = (P × 21 × 8) ÷ 100

⇒ SI₂ = (P × 21 × 21) ÷ 100

⇒ Required Ratio = SI₁ : SI₂

⇒ Ratio = [(P × 21 × 8) / 100] ÷ [(P × 21 × 21) / 100]

⇒ Ratio = (P × 21 × 8) ÷ (P × 21 × 21)

⇒ Ratio = 8 ÷ 21

**∴ The correct answer is 8 : 21.**

**__Additional Information__**

Direct Proportionality in SI

Simple interest is directly proportional to Principal, Rate, and Time individually when the other two factors remain constant.

Effective Rate of Interest

The total interest percentage for the entire period in SI is simply (Rate × Time)%. For example, 21% for 8 years is 168% of Principal.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In SI, interest is only calculated on the initial principal. In CI, interest is calculated on the principal plus any accumulated interest from previous periods.</p

questions.question: Select the INCORRECT formula from the following options.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Identify the three standard Pythagorean trigonometric identities:

1. sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

2. sec²θ − tan²θ = 1

3. cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1

Comparing these with the options, option (3) states sec²θ + cos²θ = 1, which is mathematically incorrect.

**∴ The correct answer is sec²θ + cos²θ = 1.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Four trigonometric formulas to verify.

**Formula Used:** In a right-angled triangle, Pythagoras Theorem: p² + b² = h².

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/25d058ba5a44fd3c2557235cbc3f01b3abbce916ea9786b5595d99c51ebdc780.png] 

⇒ Option 1: cosec²θ − cot²θ = (h/p)² − (b/p)² = (h² − b²)/p² = p²/p² = 1 (Correct)

⇒ Option 2: sin²θ + cos²θ = (p/h)² + (b/h)² = (p² + b²)/h² = h²/h² = 1 (Correct)

⇒ Option 3: sec²θ + cos²θ = (h/b)² + (b/h)² = (h⁴ + b⁴)/(b²h²) ≠ 1 (Incorrect)

⇒ Option 4: sec²θ − tan²θ = (h/b)² − (p/b)² = (h² − p²)/b² = b²/b² = 1 (Correct)

**∴ The correct answer is sec²θ + cos²θ = 1.**

**__Additional Information__**

Reciprocal Identities

Standard relations are sinθ × cosecθ = 1, cosθ × secθ = 1, and tanθ × cotθ = 1.

Complementary Angle Formulas

sin(90° − θ) = cosθ, tan(90° − θ) = cotθ, and sec(90° − θ) = cosecθ.

Derived Pythagorean Forms

1 + tan²θ = sec²θ and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.</p

questions.question:
Find the standard deviation of the following data (rounded off to two decimal places).

5, 3, 4, 7
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Mean (μ) = (5 + 3 + 4 + 7) ÷ 4 = 19 ÷ 4 = 4.75

Sum of squares (Σx²) = 5² + 3² + 4² + 7² = 25 + 9 + 16 + 49 = 99

Standard Deviation (σ) = √[(Σx² ÷ n) − μ²]

σ = √[(99 ÷ 4) − 4.75²] = √[24.75 − 22.5625] = √2.1875 ≈ 1.48

**∴ The correct answer is 1.48.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Data points = {5, 3, 4, 7}, Number of observations (n) = 4

**Formula Used:** σ = √[Σ(xᵢ − μ)² ÷ n]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0aaf1092761c6a77cc3a5d495416a4d673a58b94871cb38e7561a94624b8ed17.png] 

⇒ Mean (μ) = (5 + 3 + 4 + 7) ÷ 4 = 4.75

⇒ Squared deviation for 5: (5 − 4.75)² = 0.25² = 0.0625

⇒ Squared deviation for 3: (3 − 4.75)² = (−1.75)² = 3.0625

⇒ Squared deviation for 4: (4 − 4.75)² = (−0.75)² = 0.5625

⇒ Squared deviation for 7: (7 − 4.75)² = 2.25² = 5.0625

⇒ Variance (σ²) = (0.0625 + 3.0625 + 0.5625 + 5.0625) ÷ 4 = 8.75 ÷ 4 = 2.1875

⇒ Standard Deviation (σ) = √2.1875 ≈ 1.48

**∴ The correct answer is 1.48.**

**__Additional Information__**

Variance

Variance is the average of the squared differences from the mean, calculated as σ² = Σ(x − μ)² ÷ n.

Coefficient of Variation (CV)

It is a relative measure of dispersion calculated as CV = (σ ÷ μ) × 100%.

Range

Range is the simplest measure of dispersion, defined as the difference between the maximum and minimum values in a dataset.</p

questions.question: Suresh, Dinesh and Ramesh became partners in a business by investing money in the ratio of 3 : 6 : 8. If their investments is increased by 5%, 15% and 20%, respectively, then what will be the ratio of their profits for one year?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the initial investments be 300, 600, and 800 units.

Suresh's new investment = 300 + 5% of 300 = 315.

Dinesh's new investment = 600 + 15% of 600 = 690.

Ramesh's new investment = 800 + 20% of 800 = 960.

New Profit Ratio = 315 : 690 : 960 = 21 : 46 : 64 (divided by 15).

**∴ The correct answer is 21 ∶ 46 ∶ 64.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Investment ratio (S : D : R) = 3 : 6 : 8

Percentage increases = 5%, 15%, 20%

Time period = 1 year (Constant for all)

Formula Used: Profit Ratio = (Investment₁ × Time₁) : (Investment₂ × Time₂) : (Investment₃ × Time₃)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f57ba4fc325cbd06f0c498fa434dc04e76bea9b3414da7c68e0d1a4f662ff251.png] 

Calculations:

⇒ Let initial investments be 3x, 6x, and 8x.

⇒ New investment of Suresh = 3x × (100 + 5)/100 = 3x × 1.05 = 3.15x

⇒ New investment of Dinesh = 6x × (100 + 15)/100 = 6x × 1.15 = 6.90x

⇒ New investment of Ramesh = 8x × (100 + 20)/100 = 8x × 1.20 = 9.60x

⇒ Ratio of profits = 3.15x : 6.90x : 9.60x

⇒ Multiplying by 100 to remove decimals: 315 : 690 : 960

⇒ Dividing each term by 15:

⇒ Suresh = 315 ÷ 15 = 21

⇒ Dinesh = 690 ÷ 15 = 46

⇒ Ramesh = 960 ÷ 15 = 64

**∴ The correct answer is 21 ∶ 46 ∶ 64.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Partnership Profit Sharing Rule

Profit is always distributed in the ratio of the product of Capital and Time (P = C × T). If Time is constant, Profit Ratio = Capital Ratio.

Percentage Change in Ratio

If a value 'a' increases by r%, the new value is a × (1 + r/100). This can be applied directly to ratio terms.

Simplifying Ratios

To simplify a ratio involving decimals, multiply all terms by a power of 10 to convert them to integers and then divide by their HCF.

questions.question: The ratio of marks obtained by Rajesh, Rakesh and Ramesh in an exam is 2 : 4 : 9. What are the marks obtained by Rakesh and Ramesh, if Rajesh scored 30 marks in the exam?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Rajesh : Rakesh : Ramesh = 2 : 4 : 9

Given: Rajesh (2 units) = 30 marks

Unit value = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 marks

Rakesh (4 units) = 4 × 15 = 60 marks

Ramesh (9 units) = 9 × 15 = 135 marks

**∴ The correct answer is Rakesh = 60, Ramesh = 135.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of marks = 2 : 4 : 9

Marks scored by Rajesh = 30

**Formula:**

Value of one ratio part = Given value ÷ Corresponding ratio share

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/05f3a285141bae18c74686c2243811ddf085cce0ba6da445f9d56c6b7e7ccfa0.png] 

⇒ Let the marks of Rajesh, Rakesh, and Ramesh be 2x, 4x, and 9x respectively.

⇒ 2x = 30

⇒ x = 30 ÷ 2 = 15

⇒ Rakesh's marks = 4x = 4 × 15 = 60

⇒ Ramesh's marks = 9x = 9 × 15 = 135

**∴ The correct answer is Rakesh = 60, Ramesh = 135.**

**__Additional Information__**

Ratio Definition

A ratio compares quantities by division and is usually expressed in its simplest form (a : b).

Unitary Method in Ratios

Total value = (Sum of ratio parts) × (Value of one part). Conversely, Value of one part = Given value ÷ Respective ratio part.

Proportion

Equality of two ratios is called proportion. If a : b :: c : d, then product of extremes (ad) = product of means (bc).</p

questions.question: The average of 20 numbers is 32. If two numbers are 29 and 31, then what is the average of the remaining numbers (correct up to two decimals)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial average of 20 numbers = 32.

Numbers removed = 29 and 31 (Total = 60).

Deviation from average = (29 − 32) + (31 − 32) = −3 + (−1) = −4.

Since the removed sum (60) is less than the expected sum (32 × 2 = 64), the average will increase.

Net increase in average = 4 ÷ 18 ≈ 0.22.

New average = 32 + 0.22 = 32.22.

**∴ The correct answer is 32.22.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total numbers (n₁) = 20

Initial average (A₁) = 32

Numbers to be removed = 29 and 31

**Formula:** Average = Sum of observations ÷ Number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e23ddbd157f7b74cefb3fe2f5452474bdfb2ca3a5c4b071e7e959d7b59bc0354.png] 

Calculations:

⇒ Total sum of 20 numbers = 20 × 32 = 640

⇒ Sum of the two removed numbers = 29 + 31 = 60

⇒ Sum of the remaining numbers = 640 − 60 = 580

⇒ Total remaining numbers = 20 − 2 = 18

⇒ Average of remaining numbers = 580 ÷ 18

⇒ Average = 290 ÷ 9 = 32.222...

**∴ The correct answer is 32.22.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of First n Natural Numbers

The average of the first n natural numbers is given by the formula (n + 1) ÷ 2.

Effect of Replacement on Average

When a value x is replaced by y, the New Average = Old Average + (y − x) ÷ Total Count.

Weighted Average

For two groups with averages A₁, A₂ and counts n₁, n₂, the combined average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p

questions.question: The angle of elevation of the top of a building at a distance of 70 m from its foot on a horizontal plane is found to be 60°. Find the height of the building.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a 30°−60°−90° right-angled triangle, the ratio of sides opposite to the angles is 1 : √3 : 2.

Base (opposite to 30°) = 70 m.

Height (opposite to 60°) = Base × √3.

Height = 70 × √3 = 70√3 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 70√3 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance from the foot (Base) = 70 m

Angle of elevation (θ) = 60°

**Formula Used:**

tan θ = Perpendicular (Height) ÷ Base

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/661e12529d207f3072cec54e41377846508632c4b2194b9b524a51b6c07087fe.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ tan 60° = h ÷ 70

⇒ √3 = h ÷ 70

⇒ h = 70 × √3

⇒ h = 70√3 m

**∴ The correct answer is 70√3 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Values for Heights & Distances

tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, and tan 60° = √3 are the most frequently used ratios in elevation problems.

Angle of Elevation and Depression

The angle of elevation from an observer's eye to an object is numerically equal to the angle of depression from the object to the observer due to alternate interior angles.

30-60-90 Triangle Theorem

In any 30°−60°−90° triangle, the hypotenuse is twice the shorter leg, and the longer leg is √3 times the shorter leg.</p

questions.question: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral and BC is a diameter of the related circle on which A and D also lie. ∠BCA = 19° and ∠CAD = 32°. What is the measure of ∠ACD?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a cyclic quadrilateral with diameter BC, ∠BAC = 90°.

∠BAD = ∠BAC + ∠CAD = 90° + 32° = 122°.

Since ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral, ∠BAD + ∠BCD = 180°.

∴ ∠BCD = 180° − 122° = 58°.

∠ACD = ∠BCD − ∠BCA = 58° − 19° = 39°.

**∴ The correct answer is 39°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** BC is diameter, ∠BCA = 19°, ∠CAD = 32°.

**Formula Used:** Angle in a semi-circle is 90°; Sum of opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral is 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e614e83c0bd2cce93491f5d0d2cbe03a574be182f8b39b9bd88a3742d5fd7e84.png] 

⇒ In &xot;ABC, since BC is the diameter, ∠BAC = 90° (Angle in a semi-circle).

⇒ ∠BAD = ∠BAC + ∠CAD = 90° + 32° = 122°.

⇒ For cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, ∠BAD + ∠BCD = 180°.

⇒ 122° + ∠BCD = 180°.

⇒ ∠BCD = 180° − 122° = 58°.

⇒ We know ∠BCD = ∠BCA + ∠ACD.

⇒ 58° = 19° + ∠ACD.

⇒ ∠ACD = 58° − 19° = 39°.

**∴ The correct answer is 39°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle in a Semi-circle

An angle subtended by the diameter of a circle at any point on the circumference is always a right angle (90°).

Cyclic Quadrilateral Property

The sum of opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral is always 180° (∠A + ∠C = 180° and ∠B + ∠D = 180°).

Angles in the Same Segment

Angles subtended by the same arc at the circumference of the circle are equal. For example, ∠ADB = ∠ACB.</p

questions.question: Find the single equivalent discount for successive discounts of 12%, 18% and 25% on the marked price of a car.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use multiplying factors for successive discounts: (1 − d₁)(1 − d₂)(1 − d₃)

Multiplying factor = (1 − 0.12) × (1 − 0.18) × (1 − 0.25)

⇒ 0.88 × 0.82 × 0.75 = 0.5412

Single Equivalent Discount % = (1 − 0.5412) × 100 = 45.88%

**∴ The correct answer is 45.88%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Successive discounts are 12%, 18% and 25%.

**Formula Used:** Single equivalent discount for two successive discounts a% and b% = [a + b − (a × b)/100]%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4082c3ac57861f974709c45d6e4f0dd3298009e3c092f9dffc274d71bb75bb1c.png] 

Let the Marked Price (MP) be ₹100.

⇒ Price after 1st discount of 12% = 100 − (12% of 100) = ₹88

⇒ Price after 2ⁿd discount of 18% = 88 − (18% of 88)

⇒ 88 − 15.84 = ₹72.16

⇒ Price after 3rd discount of 25% = 72.16 − (25% of 72.16)

⇒ 72.16 − 18.04 = ₹54.12

⇒ Total Discount = MP − Final SP = 100 − 54.12 = ₹45.88

⇒ Equivalent Discount % = (45.88 / 100) × 100 = 45.88%

**∴ The correct answer is 45.88%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount Formula for Two Rates

If two successive discounts are a% and b%, the net discount is (a + b − ab/100)%.

Relationship between MP and SP

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) × (100 − Discount%)/100. For successive discounts d₁, d₂, d₃, SP = MP × (1 − d₁/100) × (1 − d₂/100) × (1 − d₃/100).

Effective Discount Rate

The effective discount is always less than the sum of individual discounts. In this case: 12 + 18 + 25 = 55%, but effective is 45.88%.

questions.question: Rewa has some hens and some goats. If the total number of animal heads is 100 and the total number of animal feet is 348, then what is the total number of goats with Rewa?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume all 100 animals are hens (2 feet each).

Total feet would be: 100 × 2 = 200 feet.

Excess feet count: 348 − 200 = 148 feet.

Each goat has 2 extra feet compared to a hen (4 − 2 = 2).

Total goats = 148 ÷ 2 = 74 goats.

**∴ The correct answer is 74 goats.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of heads = 100

Total number of feet = 348

**Formula Used:**

H + G = Total Heads; 2H + 4G = Total Feet (where H = Hens, G = Goats)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a9d82d02c3d89590492be49a5ee185644947907dd993e8cc53a18a412885bebd.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Average feet per head = 348 ÷ 100 = 3.48

⇒ By Alligation method, Ratio of Hens to Goats = (4 − 3.48) : (3.48 − 2)

⇒ Ratio (Hens : Goats) = 0.52 : 1.48 = 13 : 37

⇒ Total units = 13 + 37 = 50 units

⇒ 50 units = 100 animals

⇒ 1 unit = 2 animals

⇒ Total Goats = 37 × 2 = 74

**∴ The correct answer is 74 goats.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Formula for 4-legged animals

Number of 4-legged animals = (Total feet − 2 × Total heads) ÷ 2. This is derived from linear substitution.

Weighted Average Principle

The mean value (3.48) always lies between the two extremes (2 and 4). The closer the mean is to one extreme, the higher the proportion of that category.

System of Linear Equations

Problems involving two variables and two conditions (like heads and feet) can always be solved using the substitution or elimination method.</p

questions.question: If the external angle of a regular polygon is 18°, then the number of diagonals in this polygon is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Number of sides in regular polygon = 360° ÷ Exterior angle

Number of sides = 360° ÷ 18° = 20

Number of diagonals = [Sides × (Sides − 3)] ÷ 2

Number of diagonals = [20 × (20 − 3)] ÷ 2 = 10 × 17 = 170

**∴ The correct answer is 170.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Exterior angle of a regular polygon = 18°

**Formula Used:**

1. Number of sides (n) = 360° ÷ Exterior angle

2. Number of diagonals = n × (n − 3) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/28845ef899145fcb424fa4ce3572c96b2f5f0e26d4db4ef0411d55400eb6647b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Number of sides (n) = 360° ÷ 18°

⇒ n = 20

⇒ Number of diagonals = 20 × (20 − 3) ÷ 2

⇒ Number of diagonals = 20 × 17 ÷ 2

⇒ Number of diagonals = 10 × 17 = 170

**∴ The correct answer is 170.**

**__Additional Information__**

Sum of Exterior Angles

For any convex polygon with n sides, the sum of all exterior angles is always 360°.

Sum of Interior Angles

The sum of all interior angles of a polygon with n sides is given by (n − 2) × 180°.

Relationship between Angles

At each vertex of a polygon, the sum of the interior angle and the exterior angle is 180°.

Number of Diagonals Formula

The number of diagonals is calculated as ⁿC₂ − n, which simplifies to n(n − 3) ÷ 2.</p

questions.question: The number 2918245 is divisible by which of the following numbers?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Check divisibility by sum of digits: 2 + 9 + 1 + 8 + 2 + 4 + 5 = 31 (Not divisible by 3 or 9).

Check divisibility by 4: Last two digits are 45 (Not divisible by 4, so not by 12).

Check divisibility by 11: Alternating sum = 2 − 9 + 1 − 8 + 2 − 4 + 5 = −11.

Since 11 is divisible by 11, the entire number is divisible by 11.

**∴ The correct answer is 11.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Number = 2918245

**Method:** Apply divisibility rules for each option.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cc23e5c1a37f105031c26f87330ca92f9d48a313016e4a540c8be691a6bb59cd.png] 

Checking each option:

⇒ Divisibility by 3: Sum of digits = 2+9+1+8+2+4+5 = 31. Since 31 is not divisible by 3, the number is not divisible by 3.

⇒ Divisibility by 9: Since the sum 31 is not divisible by 9, the number is not divisible by 9.

⇒ Divisibility by 12: A number is divisible by 12 if it is divisible by both 3 and 4. Since it is not divisible by 3, it cannot be divisible by 12.

⇒ Divisibility by 11: Sum of digits at odd places (from right) = 5 + 2 + 1 + 2 = 10. Sum of digits at even places (from right) = 4 + 8 + 9 = 21.

⇒ Difference = |21 − 10| = 11. Since 11 is divisible by 11, the number 2918245 is divisible by 11.

**∴ The correct answer is 11.**

**__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by 3 and 9

A number is divisible by 3 or 9 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3 or 9, respectively.

Divisibility by 4 and 8

A number is divisible by 4 if its last two digits are divisible by 4, and by 8 if its last three digits are divisible by 8.

Divisibility by 11 Rule

The difference between the sum of digits at odd places and the sum of digits at even places must be 0 or a multiple of 11.

Divisibility by 6

A number is divisible by 6 if it is divisible by both 2 (even number) and 3 (sum of digits rule).</p

questions.question: The average weight of three men is increased by 4 kg when one of them, whose weight is 100 kg, is replaced by another man. What is the weight of the new man?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

New Weight = Replaced Weight + (Total Number × Change in Average)

Here, Replaced weight = 100 kg, Number of men = 3, Average increase = 4 kg

New man weight = 100 + (3 × 4)

New man weight = 100 + 12 = 112 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 112 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of men = 3

Weight of the man replaced = 100 kg

Increase in average weight = 4 kg

**Formula Used:**

Weight of new person = Weight of replaced person + (Total persons × Increase in average)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d65e192926b7d37d807de350ebc81218453bf307c99244d8e0f9dadebb2c92d1.png] 

⇒ Total weight of 3 men = 3 × Average weight (A)

⇒ Let the weights of the men be M₁, M₂, and 100 kg.

⇒ (M₁ + M₂ + 100) ÷ 3 = A

⇒ (M₁ + M₂ + New Man) ÷ 3 = A + 4

⇒ M₁ + M₂ + New Man = 3A + 12

⇒ Since M₁ + M₂ + 100 = 3A, then M₁ + M₂ = 3A − 100

⇒ (3A − 100) + New Man = 3A + 12

⇒ New Man = 3A + 12 − 3A + 100

⇒ New Man = 112 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 112 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

General Replacement Rule

When one person is replaced, New Value = Old Value + (Total Count × Increase) or New Value = Old Value − (Total Count × Decrease).

Average of Group

Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Number of observations. If the average increases, the incoming value must be greater than the outgoing value.

Effect of Adding a Member

When a person is added (not replaced), the total count increases. New Total Weight = (Old Average × Old Count) + New Member Weight.</p

questions.question:
The median of the following data will be _________.

32, 25, 33, 27, 35, 29 and 30
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Arrange the data in ascending order: 25, 27, 29, 30, 32, 33, 35.

The number of terms (n) = 7, which is an odd number.

For an odd number of terms, the median is the middle-most value.

The middle term is the 4th term in the sorted list.

The 4th term is 30.

**∴ The correct answer is 30.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Data set = {32, 25, 33, 27, 35, 29, 30}

**Formula Used:** Median = [(n + 1) / 2]th term, where n is the number of observations (when n is odd).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f54945bfc4a1006d883fbeef098ea9fb12ff8b9beb5700f957980c14f19bf36e.png] 

⇒ Count the number of observations in the data set:

⇒ n = 7 (which is odd)

⇒ Arrange the data in ascending order: 25, 27, 29, 30, 32, 33, 35

⇒ Median = [(7 + 1) / 2]th observation

⇒ Median = 8 / 2 = 4th observation

⇒ The 4th observation in the sorted list is 30.

**∴ The correct answer is 30.**

**__Additional Information__**

Median for Even n

When the number of observations (n) is even, the median is calculated as the average of the (n/2)th and (n/2 + 1)th terms.

Importance of Sorting

The data must always be arranged in either ascending or descending order before identifying the middle term; otherwise, the result will be incorrect.

Range of Data

The range is the difference between the maximum and minimum values: Range = Max − Min. For this data, Range = 35 − 25 = 10.</p

questions.question: A hemispherical bowl of internal radius 18 cm is full of liquid. This liquid is to be filled in cylindrical bottles each of radius 3 cm and height 6 cm. How many bottles are required to empty the bowl?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Number of bottles (n) = Volume of bowl ÷ Volume of one bottle

n = [(2/3) × π × R³] ÷ [π × r² × h]

n = [2 × 18 × 18 × 18] ÷ [3 × 3 × 3 × 6]

n = (2 × 6 × 6) = 72 bottles

**∴ The correct answer is 72 bottles.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Internal radius of hemispherical bowl (R) = 18 cm

Radius of cylindrical bottle (r) = 3 cm

Height of cylindrical bottle (h) = 6 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of hemisphere = (2/3) × π × R³

Volume of cylinder = π × r² × h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b6ec9ff1a6e16c970f168a72863bc310021b329d69fbd7cdc5ba3f6a2edfc7c5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume of liquid in bowl = (2/3) × π × (18)³ cm³

⇒ Volume of one bottle = π × (3)² × 6 cm³

⇒ Let n be the number of bottles required.

⇒ n × (Volume of one bottle) = Volume of bowl

⇒ n × (π × 3 × 3 × 6) = (2/3) × π × 18 × 18 × 18

⇒ n = (2 × π × 18 × 18 × 18) ÷ (3 × π × 9 × 6)

⇒ n = (2 × 5832) ÷ (162)

⇒ n = 11664 ÷ 162

⇒ n = 72

**∴ The correct answer is 72 bottles.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area (TSA) of Hemisphere

The TSA of a solid hemisphere includes the curved area and the flat circular base, given by 3πr².

Volume of Sphere

The volume of a complete sphere is double that of a hemisphere, calculated as (4/3)πr³.

Surface Area of Cylinder

Curved Surface Area = 2πrh and Total Surface Area = 2πr(h + r).</p

questions.question: Products pass successively through the hands of three traders and each of them sells his goods at a profit of 30% of his cost price. If the last trader sold the products for Rs.300, then how much did the first trader pay for them?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Each trader adds 30% profit, so the Multiplying Factor (MF) for each sale = 1.3

Successive MF for three traders = 1.3 × 1.3 × 1.3 = 2.197

Final Selling Price = Initial Cost Price × 2.197

300 = Initial CP × 2.197

Initial CP = 300 ÷ 2.197 ≈ 136.55

**∴ The correct answer is Rs.136.55 (approx).**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Profit of each trader = 30%

Number of traders = 3

Final Selling Price = Rs.300

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = Cost Price (CP) × (1 + Profit%/100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/147c0734066467f841f89d5770af6c71ab578893397b579bcf2d46be8813af61.png] 

Let the amount the first trader paid (initial Cost Price) be x.

⇒ CP of second trader (SP of first trader) = x × (1 + 30/100) = 1.3x

⇒ CP of third trader (SP of second trader) = 1.3x × 1.3 = 1.69x

⇒ Final Selling Price (SP of third trader) = 1.69x × 1.3 = 2.197x

⇒ According to the question, 2.197x = 300

⇒ x = 300 ÷ 2.197

⇒ x = 136.5498...

⇒ x ≈ 136.55

**∴ The correct answer is Rs.136.55 (approx).**

**__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value changes successively by a%, b%, and c%, the final value is Initial × (1 + a/100) × (1 + b/100) × (1 + c/100).

Net Profit Percentage

The equivalent single profit percentage for three successive profits of p% is given by [(1 + p/100)³ − 1] × 100.

Effective Rate for Two Changes

For two successive changes of a% and b%, the net change is (a + b + ab/100)%.</p

questions.question: What is the total surface area of a pyramid whose base is a square with side 8 cm and height of the pyramid is 3 cm?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Slant height (l) = √(Height² + (Side/2)²) = √(3² + 4²) = 5 cm.

Base Area = Side² = 8² = 64 cm².

Lateral Area = 2 × Side × Slant height = 2 × 8 × 5 = 80 cm².

Total Surface Area (TSA) = 64 + 80 = 144 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 144 cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Base side (a) = 8 cm, Height of pyramid (h) = 3 cm.

**Formula:** TSA = Base Area + 1/2 × Perimeter × Slant Height (l)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aab126919f12b5b799d0d752b56d144efb9a369eafc834cb418deb751a706078.png] 

⇒ Area of square base = a² = 8 × 8 = 64 cm²

⇒ Slant height (l) = √(h² + (a/2)²)

⇒ l = √(3² + 4²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5 cm

⇒ Perimeter of base = 4 × a = 4 × 8 = 32 cm

⇒ Lateral Surface Area (LSA) = 1/2 × 32 × 5 = 16 × 5 = 80 cm²

⇒ Total Surface Area (TSA) = Base Area + LSA

⇒ TSA = 64 + 80 = 144 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 144 cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Pyramid

The volume is given by V = 1/3 × Base Area × Vertical Height.

Slant Height vs Slant Edge

Slant height (l) is the height of the triangular face, while Slant edge (e) = √(h² + (d/2)²) where d is the diagonal of the base.

Regular Pyramid Properties

In a regular pyramid, all lateral faces are congruent isosceles triangles and the apex is directly above the center of the base.</p

questions.question: The breadth ‘b’ of a room is twice its height and half of its length. Find the length of the longest diagonal of the room.

**∴ The correct answer is (√21 b) / 2.**

Breadth = b

⇒ Diagonal = √(21b²/4)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of a Cuboid

The sum of the areas of all 6 faces is given by the formula 2(lb + bh + hl).

Volume of a Cuboid

The total space occupied by the cuboid is calculated as Length × Breadth × Height.

Diagonal of a Cube

If all sides are equal (l = b = h = a), the longest diagonal is simplified to √3 a.

Area of Four Walls

questions.question: What is the simplified form of the expression (1+x)(1+x²)(1+x⁴)(1+x⁸)(1-x)?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Identify the telescoping pattern of the identity (a − b)(a + b) = a² − b².

Each pair of terms doubles the power of x: (1 − xⁿ)(1 + xⁿ) = 1 − x²ⁿ.

The sequence starts with power 1 and ends with power 8.

The final simplified power will be the highest power in the product multiplied by 2.

Highest power is 8, so final result is 1 − x⁸ × ² = 1 − x¹⁶.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 − x¹⁶.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given Expression: (1 + x)(1 + x²)(1 + x⁴)(1 + x⁸)(1 − x)

Formula: (a − b)(a + b) = a² − b²

⇒ Rearranging the terms to group conjugates:

⇒ [(1 − x)(1 + x)] × (1 + x²) × (1 + x⁴) × (1 + x⁸)

⇒ (1 − x²) × (1 + x²) × (1 + x⁴) × (1 + x⁸)

⇒ [(1 − x²)(1 + x²)] × (1 + x⁴) × (1 + x⁸)

⇒ (1 − x⁴) × (1 + x⁴) × (1 + x⁸)

⇒ [(1 − x⁴)(1 + x⁴)] × (1 + x⁸)

⇒ (1 − x⁸) × (1 + x⁸)

⇒ 1 − (x⁸)²

⇒ 1 − x¹⁶

**∴ The correct answer is 1 − x¹⁶.**

**__Additional Information__**

Difference of Squares Identity

The algebraic identity (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b² is fundamental for simplifying products of binomial conjugates.

Exponents Rule

When raising a power to another power, the exponents are multiplied: (xa)b = xa × b.

General Telescoping Form

The general product (1 − x)(1 + x)(1 + x²)(1 + x⁴)...(1 + x²ⁿ) simplifies to 1 − x²ⁿ⁺¹.</p

questions.question: If the areas of two similar triangles are in the ratio 196 : 625, what would be the ratio of the corresponding sides?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For two similar triangles, the ratio of their areas is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Ratio of sides = √(Ratio of Areas)

Ratio of sides = √196 : √625

Ratio of sides = 14 : 25

**∴ The correct answer is 14 : 25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of areas of two similar triangles = 196 : 625

**Formula used:**

If ΔABC ∼ ΔPQR, then Area(ΔABC) ÷ Area(ΔPQR) = (AB ÷ PQ)² = (BC ÷ QR)² = (AC ÷ PR)²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/122ca963ce2ebdcfaf24681cde46406bc882f427a2b47ec56a6c3f37dd106060.png] 

Let the corresponding sides of the two triangles be s₁ and s₂.

Let the areas of the two triangles be A₁ and A₂.

⇒ A₁ ÷ A₂ = (s₁ ÷ s₂)²

⇒ 196 ÷ 625 = (s₁ ÷ s₂)²

⇒ s₁ ÷ s₂ = √(196 ÷ 625)

⇒ s₁ ÷ s₂ = 14 ÷ 25

⇒ s₁ : s₂ = 14 : 25

**∴ The correct answer is 14 : 25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Similar Triangles

The ratio of the perimeters of two similar triangles is equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides: P₁/P₂ = s₁/s₂.

Ratio of Altitudes and Medians

The ratio of corresponding altitudes, medians, or angle bisectors of two similar triangles is also equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Area Theorem

The theorem states that for two similar triangles, the ratio of their areas is the square of the ratio of any two corresponding linear dimensions.</p

questions.question: A speaks the truth 5 out of 7 times and B speaks truth 8 out of 9 times. What is the probability that they contradict each other in stating the same fact?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Probability A speaks truth = 5/7, Lie = 2/7

Probability B speaks truth = 8/9, Lie = 1/9

Contradiction = (ATᵣᵤₜₕ × BLᵢₑ) + (ALᵢₑ × BTᵣᵤₜₕ)

⇒ (5/7 × 1/9) + (2/7 × 8/9) = (5 + 16) / 63 = 21/63 = 1/3

**∴ The correct answer is 1/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Probability of A speaking truth, P(A) = 5/7

Probability of B speaking truth, P(B) = 8/9

**Formula:**

Probability of contradiction = P(A ∩ B′) + P(A′ ∩ B)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/092b4beadce5b5a70e01eb4243094ac4b88daf47a8695468a6e501a5af28ebfc.png] 

Probability that A lies, P(A′) = 1 − P(A) = 1 − 5/7 = 2/7

Probability that B lies, P(B′) = 1 − P(B) = 1 − 8/9 = 1/9

They contradict each other if one speaks truth and the other speaks lie.

⇒ Required Probability = [P(A) × P(B′)] + [P(A′) × P(B)]

⇒ Required Probability = (5/7 × 1/9) + (2/7 × 8/9)

⇒ Required Probability = 5/63 + 16/63

⇒ Required Probability = 21/63

⇒ Required Probability = 1/3

**∴ The correct answer is 1/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Independent Events

Two events A and B are independent if the occurrence of one does not affect the other, then P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B).

Complementary Events

The probability of an event not occurring is P(A′) = 1 − P(A).

Probability of Agreement

The probability that they agree with each other is P(A)P(B) + P(A′)P(B′), which is also equal to 1 − P(Contradict).</p

questions.question: There are two inlet pipes A and B connected to a tank. A and B can fill the tank in 32 h and 28 h, respectively. If both the pipes are opened alternately for 1 h, starting with A, then in how much time (in hours, to nearest integer) will the tank be filled?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work (LCM of 32 and 28) = 224 units.

Efficiency: A = 7 units/h, B = 8 units/h.

Work done in 1 cycle of 2 hours (A + B) = 7 + 8 = 15 units.

In 14 cycles (28 hours), work completed = 14 × 15 = 210 units.

Remaining work = 224 − 210 = 14 units. In 29th hour, A fills 7 units. Remaining 7 units filled by B in 7/8 hours.

Total time = 29.875 hours ≈ 30 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Time taken by A = 32 h, Time taken by B = 28 h.

Formula: Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

⇒ Work done in the first 2 hours (1 hour A + 1 hour B) = 7 + 8 = 15 units.

⇒ Number of such 2-hour cycles required to reach near 224 units = 224 ÷ 15 = 14.93 cycles.

⇒ Work done in 14 cycles = 14 × 15 = 210 units.

⇒ Time taken for 14 cycles = 14 × 2 = 28 hours.

⇒ Remaining work = 224 − 210 = 14 units.

⇒ In the 29th hour, Pipe A works and fills 7 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 14 − 7 = 7 units.

⇒ In the next hour, Pipe B works. Time taken by B to fill remaining units = 7 ÷ 8 = 0.875 hours.

⇒ Total time taken = 28 + 1 + 0.875 = 29.875 hours.

⇒ Nearest integer value = 30 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Negative Work (Outlet Pipes)

If an outlet pipe is present, its efficiency is treated as negative. Net work per hour = Σ(Inlet Efficiency) − Σ(Outlet Efficiency).

Pipes and Cisterns General Formula

If Pipe A fills in x hours and Pipe B fills in y hours, both together fill the tank in (x × y) ÷ (x + y) hours.

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If the ratio of time taken by A and B is a : b, then the ratio of their efficiencies is b : a.</p

questions.question: Two candidates contested an election. One of them got 64% of the votes and won by 434 votes. What was the total number of votes polled?
questions.solution:

The winning candidate got 64% of the total votes.

The losing candidate got (100% − 64%) = 36% of the total votes.

Difference in vote percentage = 64% − 36% = 28%

Given, 28% of total votes = 434

Total votes = 434 × (100 ÷ 28) = 1550

**∴ The correct answer is 1550.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Valid and Invalid Votes

Percentage Change and Base

questions.question: From the top of an upright pole 17.75 m high, the angle of elevation of the top of an upright tower was 60⁰. If the tower was 57.75 m tall, how far away (in m) from the foot of the pole was the foot of the tower?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Height difference between tower and pole (h) = 57.75 − 17.75 = 40 m.

In a 30°−60°−90° triangle, the ratio of sides is 1 : √3 : 2.

The side opposite to 60° is √3 units, and the base (distance) is 1 unit.

√3 units = 40 m ⇒ 1 unit = 40/√3 m.

Distance = (40/√3) × (√3/√3) = 40√3/3 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 40√3/3 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Height of pole (AB) = 17.75 m

Height of tower (CD) = 57.75 m

Angle of elevation from top of pole to top of tower (θ) = 60°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9ca4ccb1a473f9b71ade24fed4d7b6f8e7018df8ffadb571a41802c5a1143df3.png] 

**Formula Used:**

In a right-angled triangle, tan θ = Perpendicular / Base

**Calculations:**

Let the distance between the foot of the pole (B) and the foot of the tower (C) be x m.

The height of the tower above the pole level (DE) = CD − AB

⇒ DE = 57.75 − 17.75 = 40 m

In ΔADE, where AE = BC = x:

⇒ tan 60° = DE / AE

⇒ √3 = 40 / x

⇒ x = 40 / √3

To rationalize the denominator, multiply and divide by √3:

⇒ x = (40 × √3) / (√3 × √3)

⇒ x = 40√3 / 3 m

**∴ The correct answer is 40√3/3 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Angle of Elevation

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when looking up at an object. tan θ = Height / Distance.

Trigonometric Ratios for Standard Angles

tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3.

30°-60°-90° Triangle Rule

Sides are in the ratio 1 : √3 : 2. Side opposite 30° is x, side opposite 60° is x√3, and hypotenuse is 2x.</p
